faqs.a: You qualify for a Critical Skills Employment Permit if you hold a job offer of at least two years from an Irish employer registered with Revenue, your role is on the Critical Skills Occupations List or pays at least 68,911 euros, and you hold a relevant degree at NFQ Level 7 or higher.
faqs.q: Who is eligible for Ireland's Critical Skills Employment Permit?

faqs.a: From 1 March 2026, the standard threshold for listed occupations is 40,904 euros per year, the recent-graduate threshold is 36,848 euros, and the high-earner route for roles not on the list requires 68,911 euros. Thresholds are indexed and rise annually through 2030, so always confirm the current figure on the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment website before applying.
faqs.q: What are the 2026 salary thresholds for the Critical Skills Permit?

faqs.a: The list covers more than one hundred occupations across ICT, engineering, health, science, construction and finance. ICT roles include software developers, IT business analysts and systems designers; engineering covers civil, mechanical, electrical and chemical engineers; health includes doctors, nurses, pharmacists and therapists. Retail, hospitality and most administrative roles are ineligible.
faqs.q: Which occupations are on the Critical Skills Occupations List?

faqs.a: A benefit is that no Labour Market Needs Test is required, and after holding the permit for 21 months you can apply for a Stamp 4 permission, which allows you to work for any employer without a permit. The application fee is 1,000 euros, and processing is fast, with applications lodged in October 2026 being reached within a week.

headline: Ireland Critical Skills Employment Permit 2026: Eligibility and Salaries
metaDescription: Ireland's Critical Skills Employment Permit 2026: salary thresholds from 36,848 to 68,911 euros, eligible occupations, degree rules and the Stamp 4 pathway.

sections.content:
Ireland's Critical Skills Employment Permit is the country's main route for highly skilled workers from outside the European Economic Area. It targets occupations where Ireland faces chronic skills shortages, and it offers a faster, more flexible path to long-term residence than the General Employment Permit. Tech, engineering, healthcare, science and construction dominate the eligible list.

The permit is issued for two years in the first instance and is tied to a specific employer and role. Unlike the General Employment Permit, it requires no Labour Market Needs Test, which removes a major source of delay. Demand is strong: the permit is particularly popular with software engineers, doctors, nurses and engineers relocating to Dublin, Cork and Galway.
sections.title: What Is the Critical Skills Permit?

sections.content:
To qualify, you need a written job offer of at least two years from an employer that is trading in Ireland and registered with Revenue, and the employer must meet the 50:50 rule, meaning at least half its workforce are EEA citizens. Your role must be on the Critical Skills Occupations List, or pay at least 68,911 euros if it is not on the list but also not on the Ineligible List.

Salary thresholds from 1 March 2026 are 40,904 euros for listed roles with a relevant degree, 36,848 euros for recent graduates who qualified within twelve months, and 68,911 euros for the high-earner route. You also need a relevant qualification at NFQ Level 7 or higher, equivalent to an Irish bachelor's degree; foreign degrees require QQI recognition, which costs 170 to 200 euros and takes six to eight weeks.
sections.title: Eligibility and Salary Thresholds

sections.content:
The Critical Skills Occupations List, maintained by the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment, contains more than one hundred occupations. ICT entries include IT directors, project managers, business analysts, software developers and web professionals. Engineering covers civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, electronic and chemical engineers, plus BIM managers and quantity surveyors.

Health and science entries include doctors, pharmacists, psychologists, radiographers, physiotherapists, registered nurses and midwives, laboratory scientists and meteorologists. Business and finance entries are narrower, covering certain accountants, tax specialists and actuaries. Roles in retail, hospitality, food service, care work and most administration are on the Ineligible List and cannot use this permit.
sections.title: Eligible Occupations in Detail

sections.content:
Applications are submitted online to the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment, with a government fee of 1,000 euros. Processing is currently quick: in late October 2026 the department was working on applications received about a week earlier. You should still allow time for QQI degree recognition and for gathering contracts, payslips and qualification documents before applying.

After 21 months on a Critical Skills Permit, you can apply for Stamp 4 immigration permission, which frees you to work for any employer without a new employment permit. This makes the Critical Skills route one of the fastest paths to labour-market freedom in Ireland, and a stepping stone toward long-term residence for skilled migrants and their families.
